A role holds a set of capabilities. A user holds a set of roles. Any server route or RLS policy can ask one question: does the calling user hold this capability?

## The tables

```text
public.roles              key, label, description, is_builtin
public.role_capabilities  role_key, capability
public.user_roles         user_id, role_key
```

The migration `004_roles_and_capabilities.sql` adds them.

- A capability key looks like `posts:publish`. The literal `*` means every capability.
- The role key and the capability string are free text. A format constraint checks them. They are not an `enum`, so any layer can add its own capability in its own migration.
- The built-in `admin` role holds one row: `('admin', '*')`.
- The first account that signs up becomes an admin. It gets `profiles.is_admin = true` and the `admin` role. The database ignores any `is_admin` value in the sign-up data.

## `is_admin()` and `has_capability()`

`public.is_admin()` returns `true` for a user whose `profiles.is_admin` column is `true`, or who holds the `admin` role. The migration grants the `admin` role to every existing admin, so no data migration is needed.

`public.has_capability(cap)` is the general check. It is `true` for an admin, or for a role grant that names `cap` or `*`. Prefer `has_capability()` over `is_admin()` in new code.

The column `profiles.is_admin` stays. New code must keep writing it.

## Guard a server route

```ts [server/api/settings/update.post.ts]
import { requireCapability } from '../../utils/capability-guard'

export default defineEventHandler(async (event) => {
  await requireCapability(event, 'settings:manage')
  // ...
})
```

`requireCapability` throws 401 if the caller is not signed in. It throws 403 if the caller lacks the capability. The check runs in the database, through `has_capability()`. It reads `auth.uid()` from the session of the caller.

Other guards:

- `requireAdmin(event)`. It reads `profiles.is_admin` directly. The migrations routes use it, so no route depends on a migration that it exists to apply. There is no `system:migrate` capability.
- `requireAdminRole(event)`. It calls the rpc `is_admin()`, so it also accepts an admin who has the role only. The access routes use it.

## Client side

The layer registers a `permissionsDriver`. It reads `GET /api/permissions/me`. The route returns an empty list, and not a 500, when `my_capabilities()` does not exist yet. `usePlutoPermissions().can()` uses the list to show or hide UI.

::warning
Hiding a button is not a security boundary. The server guard, backed by RLS, is the real enforcement.
::

The layer declares the capabilities `settings:manage` and `users:read`.

## Why `profiles` has no update policy

`public.profiles` has a select policy and no update policy, on purpose. A user who could update their own row could also set `is_admin` to `true`. When a user must change one column of their own row, add a `security definer` function that writes only that column for `auth.uid()`. See [Profile language](/supabase/profile-language).

## The Users tab

The tab is at `/admin/settings/users`. It has order 10 and needs the `users:read` capability.

- It shows name and email (with a "You" badge on your row), role badges, a status (Active, or Invited with the date), and the last sign-in.
- Only an admin sees **Invite user** and the row menu. The server checks again.
- The row menu has **Edit roles**, **Resend invite**, **Copy invite link**, and **Revoke access**. Resend and copy are for pending users. Copy needs the service key.

### Invite

The invite modal has email, an optional name, roles, and the email language. The default language is the one of the admin. See [Invites and email](/supabase/invites-and-email).

### Edit roles and revoke

- **Edit roles** replaces the roles of a user. A user needs at least one role. If you remove your own `admin` role, a warning shows.
- **Revoke access** removes all roles. The account stays. The last admin cannot be revoked. The server answers 409 `lastAdmin`.

## The Roles tab

The tab is at `/admin/settings/roles`. It has order 20 and is for admins only (`*`).

The table shows the role (label, key, and a **Built-in** badge), the number of permissions (or **Full access** for `*`), the number of users, and a row menu.

The role editor has a name, a key, a description, and the permissions. The key is made from the name until you edit it. It must match `^[a-z0-9_]+$`. The permissions are grouped by layer. A role needs at least one permission. The `admin` role opens read-only. A built-in role cannot be deleted. The delete modal says how many users lose the role.

## The access API

The migration `008_users_and_roles_admin.sql` adds eight `security definer` functions with an empty `search_path`: `list_staff_users`, `list_roles`, `find_user_id_by_email`, `set_user_roles`, `add_user_roles`, `create_role`, `update_role`, and `delete_role`. The routes under `/api/access/**` call them with the session of the caller.

| Route | Guard |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/access/users`, `GET /api/access/roles` | `users:read` |
| `POST /api/access/users/invite` | Admin. Rate limit: 10 per 10 minutes for each caller. |
| `POST /api/access/users/invite-link` | Admin. Same limit. Needs the service role key. |
| `GET /api/access/capabilities` | Admin. Returns `{ serviceKey, mail: { configured } }`. |
| `POST /api/access/users/[id]/resend` | Admin. Same limit. Only while the email is not confirmed. |
| `PUT` and `DELETE /api/access/users/[id]/roles` | Admin. `DELETE` sets an empty list. |
| `POST /api/access/roles`, `PUT` and `DELETE /api/access/roles/[key]` | Admin |

Rules:

- Every write needs `is_admin()`. There is no `users:manage` capability.
- The Users list shows staff only. Staff is a user with a role, or with `profiles.is_admin`.
- A new role has no `*` and at least one capability. The `admin` role cannot be edited or deleted.
- A rule error is `P0001` with the message `pluto:<code>`. A missing right is `42501` with `pluto:forbidden`. The server maps `last_admin` and `role_exists` to 409, `forbidden` to 403, the format codes to 400, and the `*_not_found` codes to 404.

### The admin column sync

`set_user_roles(target, role_keys)` replaces the roles of a user. An empty array is a revoke. It sets `profiles.is_admin` to true when `admin` is in the list, in the same transaction. `add_user_roles` sets the column to true when it adds `admin`.

The last-admin rule: if the target is an admin, the new set has no `admin`, and no other admin exists, the function raises `pluto:last_admin`. Every role writer takes an advisory lock, so two admins cannot remove each other at the same time.

If you grant the `admin` role by hand with SQL, also set `profiles.is_admin = true`.

## Grant a role by hand

Use the Users tab when you can. You can also run SQL:

```sql
insert into public.roles (key, label) values ('editor', 'Editor')
on conflict (key) do nothing;

insert into public.role_capabilities (role_key, capability) values
  ('editor', 'posts:publish'), ('editor', 'posts:read_drafts')
on conflict do nothing;

insert into public.user_roles (user_id, role_key)
select id, 'editor' from public.profiles where email = 'someone@example.com'
on conflict do nothing;
```

## Limits

- There is no per-row ownership. A capability is all or nothing for every row of a table.
- `profiles.is_admin` and the `admin` role grant can drift apart when you write `user_roles` by hand.
